labels.label: bzthm:c3s2t3_algebre_boole_projective

hypotheses.paper: w convexe, support S(E), noyau vide
hypotheses.here: kept (1): quartS satisfies all of them and is open; (2) noyau not used (dropped)
hypotheses.note: theoreme3_ferme needs IsConvexPart w, supportK w = univ
E a real topological vector space (IsTopologicalAddGroup, ContinuousSMul), needed for « fermé »; no finite dimension
IsClosed w: the alternative domain OQ-168 names

findings: l.570–576, Théorème 3, is refuted as printed for an OPEN w: relative to the open quarter {y > 0, z > 0} of S(2) (convex, open, support S(2), noyau ∅) no distributive lattice, hence no Boolean algebra, on the distinguished subvarieties is ordered by inclusion. The three distinguished lines x = 0, x = y, x = 2y of the plane z = 0 break distributivity: x ⊓ y and x ⊓ z are ∅, while y ⊔ z contains the plane, so x ⊓ (y ⊔ z) = x (BooleProjectifDomainesInstance.not_theoreme3_ouvert, a genuine refutation named not_…, for the restatement register; also not_distribLattice_quartS). Together with not_theoreme3 (w₂: line-free, not open) this shows each of the two added hypotheses of theoreme3 (w open, F(w) line-free) is necessary: neither alone suffices.

For w CLOSED (OQ-168's alternative, « corps convexe » read as IsClosed), Théorème 3 holds but degenerately: the only conjugate pairs are (S(E), ∅) and (∅, S(E)) (estConjugueS_iff_of_isClosed), the distinguished subvarieties are exactly ∅ and S(E) (estDistingueS_iff_of_isClosed), and the Boolean algebra is {∅, S(E)} with complement the (unique) conjugate, inf ∩, sup the convex hull (theoreme3_ferme). Proved for every real topological vector space E, without the noyau hypothesis. The planner's [r] claim is confirmed.

Consequence for OQ-168: the closed domain makes Th. 3 true only because it has no nontrivial decomposition at all, so it cannot be the domain of Props. 4–5 (l.598–620), which decompose open w; the closed positive simplex of S(n) (closure of the open simplex, which has n + 1 simple ones) has exactly one simple distinguished subvariety (simplexS_simplesS, simplexS_contraste for n = 2: 3 against 1).
questions: « corps convexe » for OQ-168's alternative read only as IsClosed w (noyau and compactness not used; the result holds without them). Not resolved here: whether the author intends closed w at all; this file only evaluates that alternative.

labels.label: bzcor:c3s2t3c_algebre_parties_projective

hypotheses.note: IsClosed w (OQ-168's alternative); noyau not used

findings: l.579–590, the Corollary, holds for closed w with cardinal exactly 1: the simple distinguished subvarieties are {S(E)} (simplesS_eq_of_isClosed), the order isomorphism Set(simples) ≃o distinguished by T ↦ convex hull, and the unique representation, all proved (corollaire_algebre_parties_projective_ferme). The bracket « (n+1) au cas du n-simplexe ouvert » therefore lies outside the closed domain: the closed simplex gives 1 (simplexS_contraste).

instances: (1) the open quarter BooleProjectifInstance.quartS of S(2): convex, open, support S(2), noyau ∅ (isConvexPart_quartS, isOpen_quartS, supportK_quartS, noyau_quartS, bundled in not_theoreme3_ouvert)

(2) the closed positive simplex FacetteDualeInstance.simplexS n of S(n), every n: convex, closed, support S(n), noyau ∅, F line-free (BooleProjectifDomainesInstance.simplexS_hyps), an instance of every hypothesis of theoreme3_ferme and corollaire_algebre_parties_projective_ferme
kb_proposals: To refute « a lattice structure B on a subtype ordered by inclusion », state the lattice argument over an abstract [DistribLattice α] with f : α → Submodule and hle : x ≤ y ↔ f x ≤ f y, then apply it with @lemma _ B Subtype.val: inside a proof, letI := B does not override Subtype.instLE for `≤`, so `x ≤ y` silently elaborates to the subtype order.

For w closed in S(E), F(w) = A + A′ (ConeDec) is impossible: a ∈ A is a limit of a + t a′ ∈ F(w), so mem_F_of_forall_add_smul (Chapter3/Sature.lean) puts a in A + A′ and forces 0 ∈ A′ (Sphere.not_coneDec_of_isClosed); the distinguished subvarieties of a closed w are ∅ and S(E).
